items.q: What did the warm-vs-cold study change?
items.a: **One word** in the same description of a stranger: **warm** or **cold**.

items.q: How big was the effect on 'generous'?
items.a: **92%** rated the warm person generous vs **14%** for cold.
Yes: **369 mostly adult participants** gave results within a few points of the original.

items.q: What does warmth do to your other traits?
items.a: It **amplifies** them: people rate you wiser, funnier and more generous.

items.q: Does being seen as warm hurt perceived competence?
Why can't people believe your competence without warmth?
items.a: Because **warmth is a facet of trust**.
**Describe them warmly**: you're setting **their first impression**.

items.q: What should you audit on LinkedIn and your résumé?
items.a: Whether you have **warm words**, not just **competent** ones.

items.q: What's an easy warm habit in messages?
items.a: Sign off **warmly** in email, chat and Slack, but **only if it's authentic**.
It **undermines how people see you**; showing warmth **isn't bragging**.
